enabled.description: (#1279, B2): "1" or true judges the screen form of every turn of a person with a round: it orders the curator's view for `view_target` (`view_ask`, D58 GH #1480), asks `./screen_model` once and sends the form as a second stamp `{turn_id, audience_set, screen_form}` out of the rim on `verdict` (the presenter's `in_verdict`). "0" (shipped): it hears the turn and sends nothing.

view_target.description: D58 GH #1480: the target of the view this cell orders from the curator (`view_ask.target`) -- the name of the family in the view's system tree the domains contribute to for this judge. The cell has no built-in name (R-58-15): talky sets `decide` for the route and the screen judge alike, one family for the judgement of the composite (the presenter's screen topics, the collector's hints), and a composition that runs its judge on another model names that target here. "" orders a view without a target (the person's words alone).

view_sources.description: D58 GH #1480: which leaf of the target's family this cell reads for what, `{screen, hints}` -> the name of the contributing source: `screen` the screen topics (`[{name, purpose, candidates?: [{key, describe}]}]`, talky: `presenter`), `hints` the person's earlier how-questions (`[{question, answer, class}]`, talky: `affinity`). A role without a source, or a leaf that is no such list, reads as none.

context_turns.description: GH #1279: how many earlier turns the judge context of the screen question carries (`view_ask.turns`); read only with `enabled` "1".

context_budget_tokens.description: GH #1279: the token budget of those turns (`view_ask.budget_tokens`); hard cap 4000, 0 or less is 1500.

view_ask.description: D58 GH #1480 (was `turns_ask`): on `view_ask`, `{turns, budget_tokens, target?}` -- the view of the curator for `view_target`

system.description: on `screen_model`: the instructions of the screen question (`system.instructions`)

stamp.description: on `verdict`: the second stamp of the turn, `{turn_id, audience_set, screen_form}`, `screen_form` one of `active`, `accompanying`, `referring`, `none`

turn_id.description: the channel turn the judgement belongs to

state.description: on `view_ask`: the turn's text, carried out and back through context, so this cell keeps no state

messages.description: the keeper's turn on `in_turn`; D58 GH #1480: on `in_view`, the view's messages; on `in_verdict`, the model's answer

system.description: D58 GH #1480: on `in_view`, the view's system tree (`frame`, `topic`, the family `<view_target>`; `view_sources` names the screen leaf)

state.description: on `in_view`: the turn's text carried back

finish_reason.description: on `in_verdict`: the model's finish reason; anything but `stop` sends nothing

description.purpose: The screen judge of talky (#1279): the FORM the screen takes in a turn -- `active`, `accompanying`, `referring` or `none` -- judged by a model of its own beside the route stamp, which never waits for it. The form leaves as a second stamp of the same turn, on the rim's `verdict`, `{turn_id, audience_set, screen_form}`; the topic and the blocks stay the route stamp's (FU-0).
description.use_when: Inside talky, beside `./route` on the keeper's `turn`, switched on with `enabled` "1" where a screen reads the stamps (the presenter's `in_verdict`).
description.not_in_scope: No topic and no block: those are the decider's (`./route`, `judge_context`). No state: the turn's text rides out and back on the hop. No retry: an error, a refusal or an answer that is no form sends nothing, and the screen stays at its standard.
description.emits_meaning: view_ask: the view of the curator for `view_target` (D58 GH #1480). screen_model: the one structured call of the turn. verdict: the second stamp, only a form, only for a turn with a round; talky carries it out on `verdict`, never on `stamp`.
description.consumes_meaning: `in_turn`: the keeper's turn. `in_view`: the curator's view with the turn's text back on `hop.state`. `in_verdict`: `./screen_model`'s answer, a JSON object `{screen_form}`.
